statement: This section should be treated as the 'hard premise' of the full text; downstream chapters must not conflict with this section.
If multiple style sources exist in repository code, this section's declaration should be used as the unified constraint for merging.
If agent infers spec from existing repository, priority should be given to extracting this section content from top module, build scripts and lint configuration.
Capability items in the abstract must find corresponding implementation points in subsequent chapters: interfaces, REQ, CSR, TEST.
If 'important features not declared in abstract' exist in repository implementation, they should be backfilled to abstract and Goals during spec consolidation.
Goals should be mapped to verifiable objects: ports, registers, state machines, tests.
If agent needs to generate spec from repository, 'configurable items + implemented feature paths' should be prioritized for mapping to Goals.
Non-goals should be prioritized to constrain agent, preventing introduction of unrequired complex mechanisms.
If 'unused reserved code' exists in repository, it should not be automatically elevated to Goal unless there is explicit call path or test coverage.
Key nouns in glossary should be consistent with signal names, state names, and register field names in code.
If code naming is inconsistent with spec terminology, explicit mapping relationships should be listed in spec.
This section should be prioritized for automatic extraction from top-level instantiation relationships, file names, and package dependencies.
If module responsibilities in repository are unclear, spec consolidation should re-layer description by 'external interface + internal state ownership'.
When extracting spec from repository code, priority should be given to searching assignments in reset branch to extract reset values and initial states.
If async reset写法 exists but script/comments claim sync release, spec should retain actual behavior and record differences.
Port table should not retain '...' as final spec content; when generating spec from repository, port width parameterization sources should be supplemented.
If AXI-Lite behavior in repository is scattered across multiple always blocks, spec should unify abstraction into 'read path', 'write path', 'response path' three contract objects.
Internal handshakes like wr_fire/rd_fire should be abstracted as intermediate event descriptions in spec for enhanced readability.
If UART model or monitor already exists in repository, spec should prioritize absorbing its frame format and sampling assumptions.
For framing error/parity error/overrun, consistent descriptions should be given in both this section and test section.
Parameter definitions should be uniquely carried by package or top-level parameters, not hard-coded repeatedly in multiple modules.
If agent infers spec, both 'definition point' and 'usage point' should be listed to discover potential inconsistencies.
Each REQ should map to at least one test number; if conditions are suitable, map to a natural language property.
If generating spec from repository automatically, priority should be given to recovering REQ granularity from test naming, error code paths, and register side effects.
Both 'read/write semantics' and 'side effect semantics' should be written in spec, e.g., whether RXDATA read pops, whether IRQ_STAT is RW1C.
If side effects are scattered across multiple modules in repository, they should be unified into corresponding register items in spec.
If TX/RX are written as a merged module in repository implementation, spec should still recommend splitting into 'transmit path / receive path' two logical responsibilities.
Boundary behaviors (e.g., framing error drop/keep byte) must be consistent between this section and test section.
When automatically extracting spec from repository, this section can be inferred from file tree, build scripts, test entry points and top-level files.
If redundant/deprecated files exist in repository, only files participating in build and verification should be included in blueprint.
Explicit mapping between test entries and REQ numbers is recommended.
If testbench already exists in repository, driver task, monitor, and scoreboard interface signatures and core check logic should be prioritized for extraction.
If assert/cover/checker module already exists in repository code, it should be directly mapped to Assertions section content.
RW1C, handshake liveness, and FIFO safety are recommended priorities for property writing.
If repository has no explicit coverage, coverage items can be derived from test matrix and corner cases.
Coverage items should prioritize serving verification completeness rather than pursuing tool-specific syntax.
If repository already has scripts, this section should directly reference real commands rather than reinventing command lines.
For multi-toolchain projects, 'reference toolchain' and 'optional toolchain' can be noted.
Acceptance criteria should be divided into 'skeleton compilable' and 'function pass' two layers.
If inferring spec from repository, CI/scripts/existing test real thresholds should be prioritized.
Node design goal is 'ensure skeleton compilable first, then gradually close behavior'; do not implement all features too early in Node-00/01.
If extracting Nodes from existing repository, recovery can be done by file dependency graph, module instantiation order, and test unlock order.
